title: Inference Provider Credibility Index - Pilot for Enterprise Procurement
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Build a repeatable, telemetry-driven 'Credibility Index' that quantifies inference providers (hosted / dedicated / private) across dimensions enterprise buyers care about: uptime/availability, latency adherence, provenance/variant stability, security posture, upgrade cadence, documented fallback behavior, and economics. The index is intended as a decision aid for enterprise procurement and internal RM/solutions teams when evaluating model/vendor substitutions and reserve-capacity buy decisions.

Goals: 1) Define a compact set of signal sources and a transparent scoring methodology that maps raw telemetry and public/vendor artifacts into a 0-100 credibility score. 2) Ship a lightweight pilot dashboard and a computed index for 6 target providers (mix of open-model hosts and private deployment patterns) to validate signal fidelity and stakeholder utility. 3) Produce guidance for procurement thresholds and an integration spec for the Model Watch operations team to automate alerts when a supplier's credibility drops below thresholds.

Scope & out-of-scope: In scope: index design, data ingestion spec (telemetry, benchmark feeds, vendor SLAs, security attestations), pilot scoring for 6 providers, dashboard prototype, and short procurement playbook. Out of scope: contractual renegotiation, full legal review of vendor agreements (Legal will be consulted but not authoring the index), or automated procurement enforcement.

Signal sources and proposed dimensions: - Availability & availability trend (platform telemetry + incident history) - Latency SLO adherence (90/95th percentiles vs declared SLO) - Performance consistency (variance across load shapes) - Model version stability (frequency of breaking model updates / API contract deltas) - Security & compliance posture (published SOC/ISO attestations, KMS/HSM support) - Economic transparency (unit token price, reserved capacity price delta, overage history) - Interoperability signal (API delta count, breaking changes) - Recovery behavior (time-to-fallback, fallback coverage)

Scoring approach (pilot): normalize each dimension to 0-100; apply initial weights: availability 25, latency 20, stability 15, security 15, economics 10, interoperability 10, recovery 5. Provide a detailed weighting appendix and allow manual overrides per enterprise buyer (e.g., security-first customers can reweight).

Deliverables: 1) Index spec doc (Confluence) with signal schema and validation rules. 2) Ingestion connectors: telemetry CSV/JSON spec + sample ETL. 3) Pilot dataset for 6 providers and computed scores. 4) Dashboard mock + link to an ephemeral superset chart. 5) Procurement guidance: three recommended thresholds (green/yellow/red) and recommended mitigation actions.

Acceptance criteria: - Score computation is reproducible from raw inputs and documented. - Pilot dashboard shows per-provider breakdown and historical trend. - Field team (SRE, Solutions, Sales Eng) validates that top-3 signals align with prior procurement experiences. - Legal and Security have given feedback on signals used for classification (not final sign-off).

Risks and mitigations: - Signal quality: consolidate multiple telemetry sources and mark provenance; fallback to manual annotations when telemetry missing. - Vendor gaming: exclude vendor self-reports unless corroborated by telemetry or third-party benchmarks. - Legal sensitivity: do not publish raw negative claims; surface aggregated index and permit supplier response workflow.

Timeline (high level): Week 1-2: finalize spec, collect telemetry sources. Week 3: ingest pilot dataset and compute scores. Week 4: dashboard prototype and stakeholder review. Week 5: finalize procurement guidance and handoff to Model Watch ops.

Stakeholders: PM (Maya), Data Eng (priority), SRE (for telemetry mapping), Research (benchmarks), Legal (review), Sales Eng / Solutions (field validation).
